notes: §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR12: "When the REVERSED phrase is specified, the subsequent READ statements for the file make the data records of the file available in reversed order; that is, starting with the last record." BindOpen binds the phrase per file-name and EmitOpen passes it to the runtime; VisitOpenFileSpec is the edition arm (accepted at --std 85, COBOL0902 from 2002). After a successful open ReversedPhraseEffect calls PositionReversed, which sets the connector's standing reversal and puts the file position indicator one past the last record. Every READ of the connector goes through ReadRecord, whose target is TargetReadOrdinal over MovesBackward (the statement's direction XOR the standing reversal), so each READ selects the preceding record and the at end condition arises below the first record; OpenCore clears the reversal at every OPEN, so it lasts for the one opening that wrote the phrase. CheckOpenTapePhrase keeps the phrase to the INPUT group and to sequential organization (COBOL2211, COBOL2210), as the general format and §1985:VII.4.3.3 SR1 do ("The REVERSED phrase can only be used with sequential files."). Probed at --std 85: three fixed records come back third, second, first, then AT END with status 10, then 46; READ INTO delivers the same record to both areas; a RECORD IS VARYING file with records of 3, 10, 1 and 6 characters comes back 6, 1, 10, 3 with each length in the DEPENDING ON item; a file with two record descriptions of different sizes and a RECORD CONTAINS 2 TO 6 file with BLOCK CONTAINS 3 RECORDS come back last to first; an empty file gives at end on the first READ; a plain OPEN after CLOSE reads forward again; in OPEN INPUT F REVERSED E the phrase governs F alone. OPEN OUTPUT, I-O and EXTEND with REVERSED, and REVERSED on a relative or indexed file, are refused. The witness writes three records and reads them back last to first.

next.reason: 1985: "When the REVERSED phrase is specified, the subsequent READ statements for the file make the data records of the file available in reversed order"; 2023: "No REVERSED phrase; GR 20 lists only "open mode specification, the sharing-phrase, retry-phrase, and REWIND phrase"". The 2023 OPEN rules cover NO REWIND, SHARING and RETRY but never REVERSED; positioning rule 12 names only EXTEND and NO REWIND. The REVERSED phrase is dropped.
